title: Frictional force (ঘর্ষণ বল)
placement: Book pages 88–89, topic 3.9: ঘর্ষণ বল (Frictional Force). Next to চিত্র ৩.১৫ (a block pushed on a table: F and the friction f) and চিত্র ৩.১৬ (the microscopic roughness of two touching surfaces).
description: A red 2 kg crate is pulled by an articulated person in an orange shirt and blue trousers, leaning away and gripping a horizontal rope, in a store room: a polished blue-grey cement floor with a painted yellow lane, a powder-blue lime-washed wall over a deep teal dado, barred windows, a shelf of tins, jute sacks and wooden crates, with daylight from the windows casting soft shadows forward. Bold white-outlined arrows: orange rope tension above the crate and pink friction at its foot are equal and opposite while the crate is held; beyond the friction limit the crate accelerates, and after release friction slows it. Reverse the pull or add 1 kg weights to compare the threshold (9.8, 14.7, 19.6 N; one friction coefficient for this introductory lesson). An enlarged contact window along the bottom of the view is open by default: cyan and green particle markers follow the rough upper and lower surfaces, showing interlocking, compression and relative sliding; its 'not to scale, particles illustrative' note is in the panel, beside its switch. A qualitative warmth indicator rises during rubbing; no measured temperature is claimed. Two visible pullers alternate during the schematic back-and-forth rubbing. The panel under the view shows the weights, one guided action with pause/turn/replay, a reading box (rope tension and friction in newtons with direction glyphs, the result line, the contact switch) and a short rule. Five quiz scenes cover direction, balanced forces, weight, roughness and heating, with learning controls locked during assessment. Self-contained Three.js, Bangla first, with English and keyboard support.
